common_name: Decadence Cherries Jubilee Baptisia (Cherry-Red and Yellow Bicolor False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and resents transplanting once established; Cherries Jubilee bears striking bicolor flowers combining cherry-red and yellow tones, part of the compact Decadence series.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and does not transplant well once established. Cherries Jubilee bears dense spikes of striking bicolor flowers combining cherry-red banners with contrasting yellow wings, an unusual, vivid combination among Baptisia cultivars, part of the Decadence series bred for more manageable garden size than the sprawling wild species while keeping the genus's legendary toughness and longevity. Following bloom, dark seedpods provide fall and winter interest, and the plant serves as a larval host for several native butterfly species. It is extremely drought-tolerant and essentially maintenance-free once established. Avoid dividing or transplanting mature plants; simply cut back in late winter if a tidier form is wanted.
